routeSelection.basis: The normalized source registration is B Archeologie with teaching language Dutch. The adopted 2026–27 OER formally distinguishes the Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory from English-language Archaeology; the Dutch trajectory and its 12-EC Bachelorscriptie Archeologie are selected.

exception.reason: UCR offers artefact study, Greek archaeology and heritage. Its field courses focus on geology and environmental sampling, leaving a gap between interpreting artefacts and excavating, recording and analysing finds.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–27 Dutch-language ACASA route comprises 60 EC of first-year coursework, 78 EC of later coursework, a 12 EC individual archaeology thesis with a colloquium and 30 EC of open study. The two field schools form part of the required coursework.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Introduction to World Archaeology includes artefact cataloguing and technical drawing. Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy add material interpretation. Earth Observation and Soils & Aquifers introduce field evidence for different questions. The later art, literature and history seminars do not take archaeological finds through specialist analysis and research.

candidateAssessment.assessment: Introduction to World Archaeology includes artefact cataloguing and technical drawing. Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy add material interpretation. Earth Observation and Soils & Aquifers introduce field evidence for different questions. The later art, literature and history seminars do not take archaeological finds through specialist analysis and research.

Museum, heritage and public-memory courses give a coherent account of how objects are interpreted and exhibited. They do not extend the direct archaeological courses into specialist investigation of sites and finds.
Field geology, mapping and sampling develop transferable skills. No tested course sequence integrates excavating a site, recording context and analysing its finds.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 138 EC of required courses, a 12 EC thesis including its compulsory colloquium, and 30 EC of free academic choice. Thesis entry requires completion of all first- and second-year courses. Field School 1 requires What is Archaeology; Field School 2 requires Field School 1. Listed practicals require 85% attendance or applicable replacement work. A first-year language test and remediation when needed carry no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 48 EC. Free-choice level, overlap and approval rules apply.

componentNotes.thesis: Required 12 EC individual Dutch-language thesis, including the compulsory colloquium. The English-language thesis is the alternative for the English route, not an additional component.
componentNotes.choice: 30 EC of free academic choice, subject to level, overlap, entry and applicable approval rules.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-language Archaeology track studies past societies through material remains and landscapes. Students carry out excavations in two field schools and complete an archaeology thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers artefact study, Greek archaeology and heritage. Its field courses focus on geology and environmental sampling, leaving a gap between interpreting artefacts and excavating, recording and analysing finds.
